summary.headline: Gufic Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 23% YoY to INR252 crore with EBITDA margin at 17.7%, while FY26 PAT fell to INR63.2 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter in company history, with revenue of about INR252 crore (vs INR205 crore in Q4 FY25), EBITDA of INR44.7 crore (17.73% margin vs 13.17%) and PAT of INR20.5 crore (vs INR8 crore). Full-year revenue rose to INR940.5 crore (from INR820 crore), but EBITDA margin eased to 16.26% and PAT fell to INR63.2 crore from INR69.9 crore, reflecting Indore fixed costs, a domestic critical-care working-capital reset worth about INR22 crore of revenue, and higher overheads. Indore reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 at about 30% capacity utilisation, as committed. Management guided to about 15% revenue growth in FY27, around 18% EBITDA margin for FY27, and gross debt held at about INR400 crore.

segments.name: Indore (CMO / complex injectables)
segments.commentary: Reached 30% capacity utilisation by year-end as targeted and EBITDA breakeven in Q4. 40 tech transfers complete, 27 under development; 200-plus state FDA approvals; more than 20 Indian pharma companies use it as CMO base. Management expects Indore margin of about 31-32% at full utilisation, with overall Indore margin around 20%.

segments.name: Navsari (existing plant)
segments.commentary: Management said Navsari margin was about 20% and expects it to settle at 18-18.5% as costs rise. Navsari is building cartridge and pen GLP-1 capabilities.

segments.name: Domestic / Critical Care
segments.commentary: About 48-50% of revenue. Hospital direct-billing receivables of 140-150+ days were reset to CFA/stockist distribution, costing about INR22 crore of revenue across Q2-Q4 FY26; collections now essentially complete. Critical care growth guided at 6-8%, maximum 9%, before new launches.

segments.name: Women's health (fertility and gynaecology)
segments.commentary: Strongest year ever. Gonadotropin flagship hit its highest annual sales; a hormone launched two years ago beat its annual target and was ranked among top new launches by IQVIA. IVF expected to grow at a decent rate, with recombinant launches planned over the next two years.

segments.name: Aesthetics (botulinum toxin and fillers)
segments.commentary: Claimed the number 2 botulinum toxin brand in India at about 23% share. Toxin is about 3.5% of revenue. A Canadian in-licensed filler is targeted for launch in Q3 or Q4 FY27, India only.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record FY26 international business. Shifting from distributor-led model to holding marketing authorisations (Gufic Ireland for EU), with direct supply, out-licensing and tech transfer income. Exports about 20-22% of revenue. Approvals in Myanmar, Philippines, South Africa, Colombia, Germany, Ecuador in Q4; dossiers filed in 18 countries.

segments.name: CMO
segments.commentary: About 18-19% of revenue, boosted this year by GLP-1 contract work. Management guides to about 15-18% at peak. GLP-1 revenue not quantified.

segments.name: Nutraceutical and Ayurveda
segments.commentary: Focus on pain, arthritis and GI chronic therapies; a first-in-India formulation launched in heritage orthopaedic brand in Q4. No financials disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 15% YoY, described as an internal target that management considers achievable.
Gross margin to improve by 0.5-1% YoY, driven by mix, geography, new launches and pricing.
FY27 EBITDA margin around 18%, with 0.5-1% annual improvement thereafter and above 20% by FY30.
Gross debt to stay around INR400 crore, given higher working-capital needs; no new greenfield capex for about 2 years, with replacement capex of about INR20 crore a year.
New launches to add about INR20-25 crore net each year, with blockbuster launches potentially adding INR40-50 crore.
US FDA inspection possibly by end-FY27 after July-August batches; US operations targeted for FY28-FY29 as CMO first, then CDMO.
capex_capacity: Indore at about 30% utilisation at FY26-end, EBITDA breakeven in Q4; now moving to qualification, validation and tech transfer phase. Focus on complex injectables, depot, liposomal and suspensions.
EU GMP audit by Portuguese authority completed in early December 2025; certificate pending.
Navsari machines aged 15-20 years; replacement capex about INR20 crore per year; no greenfield capex expected for about 2 years.
INR30-35 crore invested over the last two years in GLP-1 CMO readiness (machinery, validation, dossiers).
Peptide and API backward integration: outsourced share of API reduced from about 80-85% to about 65%, target about 50% in-house over time.
demand_pricing: Critical care: volumes growing at double digits but price erosion limits value growth to about 6-8%.
Export margins to rise as products move to B2C in Africa, Southeast Asia and the Philippines, though registration and dossier costs weigh near term.
GLP-1: management called the revenue too premature to quantify; partnerships in cartridge/pen (Navsari) and lyophilised vial (Indore) with partners; role is CMO/CDMO only.
Sakar Healthcare comparison: management declined to comment on competitor margins, citing Gufic's near-term investment load in dossiers, employee costs and depreciation.
Management said R&D spend is about 8-10% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and is it operating leverage or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed gross margin gains to domestic and international reset, new launches and moving to more profitable geographies, guiding 0.5-1% YoY improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GLP-1 work a confirmed contract and how big could it be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a CMO role with partners, too premature to quantify, and not in prior projections.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR6.5 crore invested in a cooperative bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Saraswat Bank relationship of over 15 years; investment earns about 15% dividend vs about 8% borrowing cost. Total exposure about INR250 crore across fund-based, non-fund-based and term loans. Shares can be sold back at face value.

qa_highlights.question: Size of botulinum toxin revenue and capex needs for fillers?
qa_highlights.answer: Toxin is about 3.5% (plus or minus) of revenue. The filler in-licence needs no capex, as it is imported from Canada and sold in India under the partner's brand.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on top-line, margins and debt over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% revenue growth YoY; FY27 EBITDA about 18%; debt flat at about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Indore cost sit in P&L and what is the Indore vs Navsari margin split?
qa_highlights.answer: Navsari margin about 20%, expected 18-18.5%; Indore at 31-32% at full utilisation and about 20% blended.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt and cash evolve, given the analyst's cash figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said short-term debt is enough for working capital for 2-3 years; long-term debt is falling; no debt-funded projects; growth investments funded from internal cash flow.

risks_watch: Negative FY26 PAT year-on-year despite revenue growth; FY27 margin recovery depends on Indore ramp-up and cost control.
Critical care price erosion versus volume growth; collections risk from CFA shift, now said to be complete.
US FDA and EU GMP certificate timing (EU certificate pending); US CDMO start targeted FY28-FY29.
GLP-1 volumes and margins may compress as competition rises; CMO share is supported by GLP-1 this year.
Currency and Middle East disruption affecting gross margins; INR400 crore debt plus rising working capital.
Launch timing for the in-licensed filler (Q3-Q4 FY27) and new launches of aztreonam-avibactam (launched this week).
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on Indore, Q4 margins and international model; more guarded on specific numbers, declining to quantify GLP-1 revenue and US timelines, and deferring competitor comparisons. Some answers were hard to follow in the transcript, and management also declined to provide segment-level financials.
key_quotes: Revenue in Q4 was around INR252 crores, our strongest quarter ever.
We told you at the start of the year that we would reach 30% capacity utilization by year-end. We got there on target.
So as I always have been saying for the past few quarters, we expect a 15% revenue jump year-over-year.
Today, our debt is around INR400 crores, total debt, gross debt is around INR400 crores.
